title: Universe and coefficient-model invariance of completed lisse modules
statement:
Fix a scheme $X$ and a small representative $C$ of its small pro-etale site [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $\ell$ be prime and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension with its $\ell$-adic topology, valuation ring $A$ and chosen uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. The coefficient field and site may initially lie in independent universes. Let $\mathcal W_0\subseteq\mathcal W$ be universes containing $C$, its covering families, $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and a finite-dimensional $\mathbf Q_\ell$-vector-space model of $E$; all comparisons with $E$ are made in a common containing universe.

There is a field $E_0$ whose underlying set lies in the universe of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a $\mathbf Q_\ell$-algebra isomorphism $e:E_0\xrightarrow{\sim}E$. Give $E_0$ the topology transported by $e$, and put $A_0=e^{-1}(A)$ and $\varpi_0=e^{-1}(\varpi)$. Then $e$ is a topological algebra isomorphism carrying $A_0$, its power ideals and $\varpi_0$ to $A$, its power ideals and $\varpi$. In either module universe form
$$B_0=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A_0/\varpi_0^n)_C,\qquad B=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/\varpi^n)_C$$
from constant ring sheaves [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $s_0,s$ be the images of the constant uniformizers. Coefficient transport gives ring-sheaf isomorphisms $B_0\cong B$ and $B_0[1/s_0]\cong B[1/s]$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization], commuting with constant-to-completion maps, all residue projections, transitions and localization units.

For a ring sheaf $R$ write $\operatorname{Loc}_{\mathcal W}(R)$ for its module sheaves in $\mathcal W$ pro-etale locally free of finite rank, allowing varying rank and rank zero [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Enlargement from $\mathcal W_0$ to $\mathcal W$, together with coefficient transport and equivalence of small site representatives, induces equivalences of the integral and localized $\operatorname{Loc}$ categories. These equivalences commute with restriction to each site slice and with rationalization $M\mapsto B[1/s]\otimes_B M$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. In particular, an abstract locally finite free integral model and its rationalization isomorphism transport in both directions, without an embedding hypothesis; every locally finite free module and every morphism in the larger universe descends up to these equivalences.

proof.text: Choose a finite basis $(b_i)_{i<d}$ of the finite-dimensional $\mathbf Q_\ell$-space $E$. On the small set $E_0=\mathbf Q_\ell^d$ put $e((a_i))=\sum_i a_i b_i$ and transport all field operations and the $\mathbf Q_\ell$-algebra map through this bijection. Explicitly $x\star y=e^{-1}(e(x)e(y))$, $x^{-1}=e^{-1}(e(x)^{-1})$, and $1_0=e^{-1}(1)$. All algebra laws follow on applying the injective map $e$. Give $E_0$ the inverse-image topology, take $A_0=e^{-1}(A)$ and $\varpi_0=e^{-1}(\varpi)$. Thus $e$ and its inverse are continuous by the definition of this topology. For every $n$, $e(\varpi_0^n a_0)=\varpi^ne(a_0)$, so $e$ identifies the two power ideals and induces $\bar e_n:A_0/(\varpi_0^n)\simeq A/(\varpi^n)$. The formulas $[a_0]\mapsto[e(a_0)]$ commute with reduction and the maps from $A_0$. The basis and all comparisons with the possibly larger $E$ are chosen in the common containing universe. No topological classification theorem is needed: the topology on the model is transported, as required.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1); agent-written finite-basis construction for the universe clause

proof.text: First compare sheafification in the two value universes, on the fixed small site $C$. The plus theorem computes set sheafification by two plus constructions. For a small-valued presheaf $P$, a plus section is a matching family on a covering, modulo equality on a common refinement. The covering data and all the factors $P(V)$ are in $\mathcal W_0$; the products of these factors, their subsets of matching families, and the quotient of their disjoint union are therefore in $\mathcal W_0$. Viewing precisely these families and the same refinement equivalence relation in $\mathcal W$ gives the same set up to its inclusion. Repeat this for the second plus. Restriction pulls back families and the unit uses the identity covering, so the comparison is natural and fixes the unit. For rings, the underlying-set sheafification theorem identifies this with ring sheafification; addition, multiplication and units agree since their maps agree before sheafification. Consequently each small constant ring sheaf has the same model in the two universes. For abelian groups, the underlying-set theorem [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets] identifies abelian sheafification with the same plus construction, so the same argument, followed by the uniquely extended scalar action in module sheafification, applies to presheaves of modules over a small ring sheaf.

proof.text:
Apply functoriality of constant sheafification to $\bar e_n$ and its inverse. The resulting ring-sheaf isomorphisms $c_n$ commute with all transitions and the maps from the constant integral ring. The sectionwise inverse-limit description gives
$$c_U((x_n)_n)=(c_{n,U}(x_n))_n,$$
with inverse $(y_n)_n\mapsto(c_{n,U}^{-1}(y_n))_n$. Transition compatibility makes these maps land in the compatible tuples. They are natural in $U$, preserve ring operations coordinatewise, and satisfy $\pi_n c=c_n\pi_{0,n}$. The constant-to-completion map sends $a_0$ to its residue tuple, whose image is the residue tuple of $e(a_0)$; in particular $c(s_0)=s$. This also proves that $B_0$ has small section sets: it is a subset of a countable product of small sets. The model for $B$ is its isomorphic copy. By step 2 the same description works in either value universe; hence the completion comparison fixes every residue projection and constant-to-completion map.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), with sectionwise inverse limits as specified in def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit

proof.text: On each object, localization sends a fraction $b/s_0^k$ to $c(b)/s^k$, with inverse $a/s^k\mapsto c^{-1}(a)/s_0^k$. These formulas respect the fraction equivalence relation: multiplying an equality by a power of $s_0$ is carried to multiplying its image by the same power of $s$. They commute with restrictions, and send $b/1$ to $c(b)/1$. Sheafify the inverse presheaf maps to obtain $c':B_0[1/s_0]\simeq B[1/s]$. Thus $c'j_0=jc$ for the localization units. Before sheafification the small localization is a quotient of $B_0(U)\times\mathbf N$; step 2 makes its sheafification small as well, in either universe. This argument requires neither injectivity of the localization unit nor a nonzero-divisor assumption on $s$.

source.place: Ringed-section localization construction used in the item; explicit fraction calculation, agent-written

proof.text:
Let $R$ be either of the small ring-sheaf models just constructed. A locally finite free $R$-module $M$ in $\mathcal W$ has small section sets up to bijection. Indeed, for each $U$ choose a small trivializing covering $(V_i\to U)_i$, with $M|_{V_i}\simeq R|_{V_i}^{r_i}$, $r_i\in\mathbf N$. Restriction and these coordinates give an injection
$$M(U)\longrightarrow\prod_i R(V_i)^{r_i}.$$
Injectivity is precisely the uniqueness part of the sheaf axiom. The product and every subset of it lie in $\mathcal W_0$, so take its image $S_U$ and the induced bijection $h_U:S_U\simeq M(U)$. There are only small many objects $U$, hence these choices can be made simultaneously in the common universe. No bound on the ranks across the covering is used. If the covering is empty, its product is a singleton and the same sheaf uniqueness argument still applies.

source.place: Definition 6.8.3; agent-written section-cardinality argument using local finite freeness and the sheaf axiom

proof.text: Make $N(U)=S_U$ into a small module presheaf by transporting the operations and restrictions through $h_U$: for $f:V\to U$ set $N(f)=h_V^{-1}M(f)h_U$, and set $a\cdot x=h_U^{-1}(a\cdot h_U(x))$. The same formula transports addition and zero. The presheaf and module laws follow by cancelling the bijections. A matching family in $N$ maps under $h$ to one in $M$; its unique gluing pulls back under $h_U$. Thus $N$ is a sheaf and $h:N\simeq M$ is an isomorphism of module sheaves after inclusion. Its restrictions to the trivializing slices are finite free, so $N$ is in the smaller $\operatorname{Loc}$ category. For small module sheaves $N,N'$, any larger-universe morphism is a family of functions between small sets indexed by the small object set of $C$. Each function is its graph, a subset of $N(U)\times N'(U)$, and the family belongs to $\mathcal W_0$. Naturality and linearity are the same equations in both universes. The inclusion is therefore fully faithful and, by the constructed $N$, essentially surjective. On morphisms between chosen small models the inverse is explicitly $h_{M'}^{-1}fh_M$; it respects composition. This establishes the equivalence, rather than only objectwise smallness.

source.place: Definition 6.8.3; explicit inverse to the fully faithful common-universe inclusion, agent-written

proof.text: A ring-sheaf isomorphism $c:R_0\simeq R$ gives scalar transport by keeping the abelian sheaf and defining $a\cdot m=c^{-1}(a)m$. The scalar-extension lemma identifies this functor naturally with extension of scalars; applying it to $c^{-1}$ gives its inverse. On a trivializing slice $R_0^r$ the coordinate map $(x_i)\mapsto(c(x_i))$ identifies its transport with $R^r$, including $r=0$. Thus $c$ and $c'$ restrict to equivalences of the integral and localized locally finite free subcategories. An equivalence $F:C\simeq D$ of small representatives with their transported covering families acts on ring and module sheaves by precomposition. Its quasi-inverse and the unit and counit give inverse functors and their isomorphisms. Matching families correspond under $F$ and its quasi-inverse, so the sheaf axioms correspond; a trivialization on a covering corresponds to one on its image covering. This proves the analogous equivalence for changing representatives, including varying ranks. On slices use the induced equivalence $C/U\simeq D/FU$. For universe inclusion, coefficient transport and this reindexing, the restriction map on sections at $V\to U$ is exactly the already specified map at $V$. For independently chosen small models on a slice, the comparison at $V/U$ is $h_{V/U}^{-1}h_V$; these maps commute with restrictions by cancellation of $h$, and their composites on iterated slices are the same formula. Thus the equivalences commute naturally with slice restriction, including for the chosen inverse functors.

source.place: Tag 03CZ lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict, invertible-map specialization; agent-written reindexing under an equivalence of small site representatives

proof.text:
Write $S_0=B_0[1/s_0]$ and $S=B[1/s]$. For the coefficient square $c'j_0=jc$, the comparison between rationalization and scalar transport is induced before sheafification by
$$S\otimes_B T_cM\longrightarrow T_{c'}(S_0\otimes_{B_0}M),\qquad a\otimes m\longmapsto c'^{-1}(a)\otimes m.$$
Its inverse sends $a_0\otimes m$ to $c'(a_0)\otimes m$. Balancing is respected since $c'^{-1}(j(b))=j_0(c^{-1}(b))$; both composites fix pure tensors. The maps commute with restrictions and all module maps, so the sheafified maps are mutually inverse and natural. Universe enlargement preserves the same tensor by the common-universe tensor comparison, whose pure-tensor formula is unchanged. For reindexing by an equivalence of representatives the sectionwise balanced tensor is the same tensor at the reindexed object, and precomposition carries the sheafification universal property to itself using the inverse equivalence. Hence its tensor comparison also fixes pure tensors. These comparisons commute with slice restriction by those formulas. Locally, rationalization of $B^r$ is $S^r$, by the inverse maps $a\otimes(b_i)\mapsto(ab_i)$ and $(a_i)\mapsto\sum_i a_i\otimes e_i$; thus rationalization stays in the stated subcategories. Finally apply these equivalences to an abstract pair $(M,\theta:S\otimes_BM\simeq L)$. Composing the transported $\theta$ with the tensor comparison transports the pair forward; the inverse equivalences transport it back. Full faithfulness transports every morphism and its inverse, so the isomorphism condition is preserved in both directions. No embedding of $M$ into $L$ is used.
